Legion is a turn-based battle between tw: Legion is a turn-based battle between two teams on a hexagonal arena. <0>Defeat every opposing character to win.</0> You begin with {{value0}} characters; your roster can eventually grow to {{value1}}.

When it is your turn, the active charact: When it is your turn, the active character is selected for you. The blue tiles show where they can move. Choose <0>one action</0>: move, attack, cast a spell, use an item, or pass. You do not move and then attack in the same turn.
The standard turn timer is <0>{{value0}}: The standard turn timer is <0>{{value0}} seconds</0>. Plan while other characters act and watch the hourglass for your remaining time. If the timer runs out, you lose that opportunity to act.
Combat starts once everyone has loaded t: Combat starts once everyone has loaded the arena and both teams’ spell and item effects. Practice matches pause if your connection drops and resume after the arena is ready again, keeping your remaining turn time. Once a match against another player has started, its clock keeps running if you disconnect.
The turn-order portraits along the botto: The turn-order portraits along the bottom of the arena, showing class crests and the sequence of characters about to act.
The turn order is your planning tool. Sp: The turn order is your planning tool. Speed and the recovery time of each action affect when a character acts again.
Class crests appear on both side rosters: Class crests appear on both side rosters and the turn order: an amber sword for Warriors, a mint cross for White Mages, and a violet flame for Black Mages.
Hover a character on the battlefield, ei: Hover a character on the battlefield, either side roster, or the turn order to highlight the same character in all three places. Their side card and turn-order portrait brighten and grow slightly, while their battlefield sprite glows. The inspection card shows their class, current and maximum HP and MP rounded to whole numbers, and active status effects with their remaining duration (∞ means permanent). You can also focus the side cards or turn-order portraits with the arrow keys or controller. Press Escape to dismiss the card.

Click an empty blue tile. Moving uses yo: Click an empty blue tile. Moving uses your action, so pick a position that sets up your next turn or gets a vulnerable character out of danger.
Click an adjacent enemy for a melee atta: Click an adjacent enemy for a melee attack. Clicking a distant enemy moves you toward them instead; it does not grant a free attack.
Choose a spell in the bottom action bar,: Choose a spell in the bottom action bar, check its highlighted area, then click a valid target or tile. Casting spends MP.
Click an equipped consumable. Self-use i: Click an equipped consumable. Self-use items such as Potion and Ether activate immediately; targeted items ask you to choose a target.
Click <0>Pass Turn</0> beside the hourgl: Click <0>Pass Turn</0> beside the hourglass timer or press <1>E</1> / <2>End</2> to give up this action. A deliberate pass recovers sooner than a timeout.
Clicks outside the targeting range are i: Clicks outside the targeting range are ignored. Choose another target, or press <0>Esc</0> to cancel targeting and move or pass instead.

Green is HP (health); blue is MP (magic): Green is HP (health); blue is MP (magic). The bar shows what this character can use, not everything in your shared inventory.
Blue mana bars show remaining MP for bot: Blue mana bars show remaining MP for both teams. Watch enemy mana to judge which spells they can still afford; casting spends MP and Ether restores it.
Let sturdy fighters approach first. Keep: Let sturdy fighters approach first. Keep your healer out of easy melee range, leave space between allies against area spells, and concentrate damage on a vulnerable enemy.
Check the order before committing: can a: Check the order before committing: can an enemy finish your injured character before your healer acts? Sometimes a Potion now is worth more than another attack.
Read item and spell details in Team or S: Read item and spell details in Team or Shop before a match: check the effect, MP cost, and action speed. Fast actions bring your next turn around sooner than slow ones. A bigger spell is not always the better choice.
<0>Check the whole target area.</0> Area: <0>Check the whole target area.</0> Area spells can affect allies as well as enemies, and healing can help an opponent caught in the area. Aim carefully before confirming.
Leaves burning ground. Crossing flames o: Leaves burning ground. Crossing flames or remaining on them causes damage. Move out of the fire; an ice spell can extinguish it.
Creates obstacles and can freeze a chara: Creates obstacles and can freeze a character in place. Break the ice with a melee attack from another character or melt it with fire. Attacking an occupied ice tile can also hurt its captive.
Deals damage over time. Cure it with an: Deals damage over time. Cure it with an equipped Antidote or Remedy instead of letting repeated damage pile up.
Prevents spellcasting. A Bocca or Remedy: Prevents spellcasting. A Bocca or Remedy removes it; a silenced mage can still move, attack, or use an item.
Prevents actions while it lasts. Thunder: Prevents actions while it lasts. Thunder spells can inflict it. Protect the affected character until they can act again.
At zero HP, a character is knocked out a: At zero HP, a character is knocked out and cannot act. A revival item such as Clover targets a fallen character; ordinary healing is not a substitute. The battle ends if your entire team is down, so revive before that happens.

<0>Equip consumables.</0> Select a chara: <0>Equip consumables.</0> Select a character, click a consumable in the shared inventory, then choose <1>Equip</1>. It fills a free carried-item slot. A Potion restores HP; Ether restores MP. Each use consumes one item. Refill after battles.
<0>Teach spells deliberately.</0> Select: <0>Teach spells deliberately.</0> Select the intended character, click a compatible scroll in the shared inventory, and choose <1>Learn</1>. <0>Fit equipment.</0> With your characte: <0>Fit equipment.</0> With your character selected, click equipment in the shared inventory and choose <1>Equip</1>. Check class and level requirements. Equipment adds passive bonuses and can be swapped between battles.

On Play, choose the golden rook to the r: On Play, choose the golden rook to the right of Ranked. Choose Balanced or Control, set the difficulty, and use Begin expedition in the bottom bar. Rules & rewards opens the full rules.
Choose <0>The Cinder Tower</0> on Play f: Choose <0>The Cinder Tower</0> on Play for an online solo expedition. A temporary Warrior, White Mage, and Black Mage climb six floors, ending with the Cinder Warden. Turns have no deadline, so the combat dock shows no timer. Enemies have boosted health, mana, attack, defenses, and speed. Your main roster and owned consumables are separate from this squad.
The tower route screen with the expediti: The tower route screen with the expedition squad, banked rewards, and a choice between the Broken Gate and the more dangerous Ember Approach.
Follow your ascent on the left. Check yo: Follow your ascent on the left. Check your squad, compare the enemy lineups, and choose your next encounter. Dangerous paths award 25% more gold and XP.
After each victory, choose one preparati: After each victory, choose one preparation: recover, refill supplies, or take an upgrade. Spell lessons fill up to three slots and replace the oldest spell when full. Upgrades last only for this expedition. Sculptor of Ice makes Ice cost 15 less MP but halves its damage; Light Footwork gives the Warrior an extra movement tile and 12 Speed.
Between victories, each ally is brought: Between victories, each ally is brought to at least 30% HP, then restores 15 HP and 15 MP, capped at their maximums. Knocked-out allies return and statuses clear. Sanctuary fully restores HP and MP; Quartermaster refills supplies. During Tower battles, ice traps thaw after two skipped turns, so a frozen squad can recover.
The combat badge shows your current floo: The combat badge shows your current floor. In Ember Approach, two fire mages stand beyond a wall of flame spanning the arena. Cast across it, or extinguish a section with Ice to cross safely.
The Warden marks tiles before its next t: The Warden marks tiles before its next turn. Move away from those warning symbols before the blast. It leaves fire behind; the turn order shows when it will act.
Gold, XP, and milestone items are banked: Gold, XP, and milestone items are banked after each victory. XP is shared across your permanent roster. Defeat or retirement ends the run but keeps everything already banked. Higher floors pay more. Clearing a tier unlocks the next, up to Tier 5; each tier adds 15% enemy HP and attack power and 20% account rewards. Your first clear also unlocks the Control starting kit.

Choose a spell in the centre of the bott: Choose a spell in the centre of the bottom command dock, check its highlighted area, then click a valid target or tile. Each spell shows its MP cost; casting spends MP.
